findings.finding: Opens 'We did not replicate the three simulation headlines of Chen (2021), who reported biased direct-effect estimates, percentile bootstrap intervals that cover the true value far too rarely, and power for the mediated interaction (MINT) near zero: 85.42% ... against 0.00% ...; 43.62 ... against 0.04; ... 0.013 (raw 0.063) ... against 0.802 (raw 0.852).' Verdict, cited source, original findings and all paired headline numbers in one sentence; the headline missed and the sentence says so.

H4 'holds only in part' with 86.3%/89.2%; limit sentence on restricted-use Head Start data and unseeded bootstrap follows; tolerances and 'point-estimate comparisons, not equivalence' closes. No reversal exists and none is invented.

Polish: 'the three simulation headlines' reads as if there were only three; H4 is also a simulation headline (Section 1 calls it 'Her fourth headline'). Not misleading in substance because H4 is reported in the next sentence and in Table 1 row E5; suggest 'three of her four simulation headlines'.

Opens 'We did not replicate the simulation headlines of Chen (2021)' with 85.42% vs 0.00%, 24.10-83.99% vs 94.6-95.6% coverage, 0.063 vs 0.852 (0.013 vs 0.802 above .05); then MC standard errors (.007; .002), H4 'holds for most but not all cells', the limit (Head Start, unseeded bootstrap) and 'No estimate reverses its sign.'
Tolerances restated (half a unit of her last decimal; figure-reading error) and labelled as point-estimate comparisons, not equivalence tests.

Polish: 'The disagreements therefore arise in steps she did not print' is slightly stronger than Section 6.1, which attributes much of the disagreement to the data behind her published runs (a run differing from the printed code); consider 'in steps or runs she did not print'.

Should-fix (non-failing): '(1,270 datasets, of which the 635 kept by the replay were compared)' is unexplained and attributes the 635 to 'the replay'. In r-reproduction/chen_exact.R the literal check deliberately keeps every other dataset of block 0 to test that skipping preserves data and RNG state; the full 1,000-replication replay keeps all 1,280,000. Table 2 (p. 6) says identity was 'verified on the first simulation block (1,270 datasets)'. Neither statement is false (RNG state over all 1,270; values over 635), but a reader can wrongly infer the replay keeps half the datasets. Fix: 'the check rebuilt every other dataset (635) and skipped the rest; the 635 are identical and the random-number state after all 1,270 is identical', and align Table 2.
Defines MINT, RDD, HSIS, PNDE/TNDE on first use; no references to earlier drafts, reviewers or internal roles; every evidence pointer is an exact filename.

Reproduction recipe separated from scientific prose; names README section 'Reproduce'; says outputs not committed and source PDF must be downloaded. Only 'master' is named; no commit hash or working branch anywhere (commit_refs.py accepted).
